body.cap: Chang Joon Yang, CEO of Marketon, delivers a pitch during the Global Media Meetup with Ubergizmo, held on July 3 at the MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Marketon Inc. (CEO Chang Joon Yang) participated in the “Global Media Online Meetup” jointly hosted by Ubergizmo, a U.S.-based tech media outlet, and AVING News on July 3. The event targeted Korean companies and startups aiming to enter the global market.

The meetup focused on introducing innovative Korean products and technologies to global media, with an emphasis on startups applying for the CES 2026 Innovation Awards. It aimed to create early exposure and business opportunities through international press coverage.

Marketon is a technology company leading the immersive XR industry with its hovering hologram display technology. Unlike conventional AR or VR that requires glasses or headsets, Marketon’s solution offers a more practical and user-friendly way to experience immersive content. Its applications span museums, smart schools, tourism signage, futuristic vehicles, and automated information systems in landmark buildings.

Marketon’s technical capabilities have been proven through various accolades: the ICT Innovation Award from the Ministry of Science and ICT (April 2024), the “NextRise Innovator” award (June 2024), and selection for the Future Innovation Award (October 2024). The company has also been designated as an “Innovative Product” by the Korean Public Procurement Service and holds certifications such as KC, FCC, and UKCE.

While demand for immersive visuals is rising, traditional immersive displays have struggled due to side effects like dizziness. Marketon’s solution offers immersive visuals without the need for VR goggles and enables interaction with floating images, which also minimizes virus transmission via contact.

body.cap: Marketon’s 12-inch mobile hologram | Image courtesy of Marketon

body.x: Compared to other immersive content technologies, Marketon’s holograms offer superior dimensionality. When used in educational settings like museums or classrooms, they help students better understand complex topics like astrophysics or theoretical physics. The product also integrates with AI tools such as ChatGPT to offer interactive services. Unlike other holograms, no lighting adjustments are needed to view the floating images, making it ideal for future display technologies.
Users can manipulate the floating images in mid-air with gestures—zooming, rotating, and dragging—which creates a captivating experience, particularly for tech-savvy younger generations.

In contactless environments, such as during pandemics, Marketon’s technology proves especially valuable. It can replace touch-based interfaces in hospitals, elevators, kiosks, and ticketing systems. The floating holograms allow for safe interaction without physical contact, potentially reducing virus transmission.

Since 2023, Marketon has mass-produced its hovering hologram products for use in education, automotive, premium cinemas, finance, public institutions, and exhibitions. Clients include Seodaemun Museum of Natural History, the Metaverse Experience Center, the National Youth Bio Center, Hyundai Motor Company, and Shinhan Bank.

In July 2025, Marketon launched its B2C product: the “Mobile Hologram,” targeting K-pop fans. This product integrates AI Agent and holographic display technologies into a smartphone-sized device capable of projecting 3D visuals in mid-air without touch. It will debut at CES 2026 to expand into the global fandom market.

body.cap: Marketon’s Mobile Hologram in action | Photo courtesy of Marketon

body.x: The Mobile Hologram leverages Marketon’s certified contactless display technology and is optimized for K-pop artist content. Users can experience artist performances, interviews, and fan meeting videos in 3D without any additional hardware. Built-in AI Agents allow users to control the content via voice or gesture, receive personalized recommendations, and even create custom playlists.

Internationally, Marketon’s solution has already been deployed to the Brooklyn Chamber of Commerce and the Asian Art Museum in San Francisco. It was also delivered to Singapore’s OCBC Bank in May 2025. Marketon is now active in Germany, France, and Malaysia, with total exports across five countries reaching more than $100k in 2024.

To further scale, the company plans to target premium education markets in the U.S., Singapore, Germany, France, and the UK. It will intensify global marketing efforts across Asia (centered in Singapore), Europe (Germany), the Middle East (Dubai), and North America (New York).

As part of this strategy, Marketon will participate in IFA 2025 (September 7-9), launching a 7-inch Mobile Hologram for the European K-pop fanbase. At GITEX 2025 (October 13-17), Marketon plans to enter the Middle Eastern market through partnerships with expo organizers.

Finally, at CES 2026, Marketon will focus on entering the North American market, especially targeting museums in New York and educational institutions in San Francisco and Los Angeles. The company already has partners in New York and Silicon Valley and plans to build up its market presence in collaboration with them.

body.cap: Chang Joon Yang, CEO of Marketon (right), and Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo (left), pose for a photo at the Global Media Meetup held on July 3 in Seocho-gu, Seoul | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo operates the Silicon Valley Post and publishes content in six languages across 200 countries, with a focus on electronics and technology. It regularly covers major global exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen attended the event. He previously worked as an NVIDIA programming engineer, developer education program manager, and 3D graphics programmer. He covers products and technologies from around the world at CES each year.
